profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading: This building is Equinix's DC15 facility on Equinix's Ashburn, Virginia campus, part of what Data Center Dynamics has called the birthplace of the commercial internet: AOL built the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support dial-up internet operations, and the fiber infrastructure that project attracted helped trigger the region's growth into Data Center Alley in Loudoun County, now described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix established its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and DC2, which followed, has been described by Data Center Dynamics as reputedly the most connected building on earth; Equinix's own published specifications for DC2 describe a single-story, reinforced-concrete, 118,446-square-foot facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load, N+1 cooling redundancy, a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment, and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High. Equinix has continued expanding the Ashburn campus well beyond DC1 and DC2, eventually building out numbered facilities into the twenties as demand grew, with Data Center Frontier reporting on Equinix's plans for a fleet of four-story buildings as part of that expansion. Equinix positions the Ashburn campus as serving one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, offering colocation in private cages, smart-hands support, managed solutions, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, cross-connects, and its own Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products. Equinix's own website confirms this building's address and IBX facility code but, consistent with the rest of Equinix's public site, does not publish this specific building's power capacity or square footage beyond the DC2 example cited above as representative of the campus's general specifications.

profile.regional_context: Ashburn's Data Center Alley, anchored historically by AOL's 1997 Dulles Technology Center and Equinix's own late-1990s DC1/DC2 buildings, is described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet, and Equinix's Ashburn campus serves one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast.

reading.body:
DC15 is a 115,604-square-foot facility in Ashburn's Data Center Alley, part of Equinix's multi-building campus in Loudoun County. Equinix does not publish DC15's power capacity or specific certifications, though the broader Ashburn campus is positioned to serve one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast and historically anchors the region's roughly 10 million square feet of total data center space. Without disclosed megawatts, no estimate of AI training rack density can be made for this building.

Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities, but only 23 publish power capacity; those 23 total 1,375 MW. Equinix Ashburn DC15 is not among the published figures. The operator's own Ashburn DC2, described as representative of the campus's general specifications, declares a minimum cabinet density of 4 kVA and N+1 power redundancy, but these specifications are not confirmed for DC15 itself.

The absence of published capacity makes this building's significance to AI scaling opaque from available data. Data Center Alley's historical role in internet infrastructure and Equinix's dense interconnection footprint matter only if DC15's power allocation to compute-intensive workloads becomes visible; the current specifications disclose no basis to assess that.
